subject: PLG grant applied but charged on Nov invoice — VAT/tokens clarification
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@blueharbor.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: accounts@blueharbor.com
Date: 2027-12-01T09:12:00+01:00
Subject: PLG grant applied but charged on Nov invoice

Hi Jonas,

We signed up via the self-serve PLG flow in mid-November and accepted the welcome grant that showed up in the console. Our engineers started a couple of test runs, but this morning our accounting team flagged an actual charge on the Nov 30 invoice for ~3.2M tokens. They expected that usage to be covered by the grant.

Can you help clarify:
- Why this usage hit an invoice vs drawing from the grant?
- Our finance team also sees a VAT line on the invoice — we are an EU company with a UK VAT ID, so we expected the supply to be reverse-charged.

Attaching the invoice (invoice-20271130.pdf) and a screenshot of the grant banner.

Appreciate a quick clarification — we’re trying to reconcile before month-end close.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform, BlueHarbor

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Samira Khan <samira@blueharbor.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-01T10:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: PLG grant applied but charged on Nov invoice

Hi Samira — thanks for the heads-up and sorry for the panic. Looping in Marissa (Billing) and Monica (CS).

Quick notes while they dig in:
- I’ve asked Billing to confirm whether the self-serve grant was attached to your org ID or to the initial project token. Sometimes grants are issued at the account level but usage is billed to a specific billing profile if it wasn’t explicitly applied.
- VAT: we usually reverse-charge for EU companies with a valid VAT ID, but a mismatch on the tax ID or billing country can cause VAT to appear.

Marissa / Monica — can you review the attached invoice and the grant record (link above) and advise next steps? If the usage should have been deducted from the grant, can we either apply a credit or issue a corrective PO? BlueHarbor is mid-PO cycle so a quick remediation would help.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, Samira Khan <samira@blueharbor.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-01T11:42:00+01:00
Subject: Re: PLG grant applied but charged on Nov invoice

Hi Samira — I pulled the invoice and the grant record. Two findings:
1) The self-serve grant was issued to the org but it arrived in the console after Nov 29 23:50 UTC; your first heavy usage window (and token spikes) happened ~Nov 29 22:30–23:20 UTC and were billed under the billing profile that was active at the time. Because the grant activation timestamp is later than the usage, the billing system did not apply it retroactively.
2) On VAT: our system used the billing country on file (GB) which normally triggers reverse-charge when we have a valid EU VAT ID, but the VAT field on the invoice was populated because the VAT ID provided in the sign-up form had an extra character (a trailing space) during validation and failed the automated validation check. We can correct both items, but we need to agree on the remediation approach.

Options we typically offer:
- Apply an account credit for the billed tokens (preferred) — we can post a credit note and offset it against the Nov invoice, leaving the invoice status as corrected.
- Issue additional free credits to cover the exact token delta if accounting cannot accept a retrospective credit note.

If you prefer a tax-only fix, we can reissue the invoice with the VAT reversed (reverse charge) once we have a validated VAT ID. We’ll need the exact VAT ID string as you’d like it to appear.

I can prepare a corrective credit note and a reissued invoice. Which would you prefer?

Marissa Cole
Billing Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira@blueharbor.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-01T13:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: PLG grant applied but charged on Nov invoice

Thanks Marissa — that makes sense. Our accounting prefers a corrective credit note plus a reissued reverse-charge invoice (so their ledger shows the tax reversal). VAT ID is GB999999973 (that was entered but I’ll resend the exact string).

BlueHarbor would accept a short-term grant top-up for the delta if that’s easier operationally, but parity in the ledger is important for our auditors.

If you can post the credit note and reissue the invoice before Dec 3 close of books, that will do.

Samira

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Samira Khan <samira@blueharbor.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-03T15:40:00+01:00
Subject: RE: PLG grant applied but charged on Nov invoice

Samira — quick update and remediation plan.

1) Credit note: we generated credit CN-2027-BH-1145 for the token charges and applied it to invoice INV-2027-11-30. The credit will show on your account and we will send the reissued invoice (INV-2027-11-30-RC) with reverse-charge VAT lines suppressed. Link: https://app.redwood.ai/invoices/BH-2027-11-30
2) Grant top-up: as a gesture and to avoid interrupting engineering work, I approved a one-off 5M token promotional grant to BlueHarbor. This will appear in the console as an account-level credit and can be consumed immediately. Details and terms (selfserve-grant-terms.pdf) are attached. Note: promotional grants do not alter the bookkeeping for the original invoice — the credit note is the formal accounting remediation.
3) Next steps for future signups: I’ve asked Product to flag grants with an "effective_from" timestamp and to add a console notice for "grant pending activation" when the grant is being provisioned to avoid the timing gap.

Let me know if you need the corrected VAT ID displayed differently; otherwise we will proceed with the reissue.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
